quests.title: The Gate of Hearthglen
quests.description: Walk up the King's Road and look at Hearthglen's gate, without starting a fight.
quests.accept_text:
I'm Lena Fischer, and I keep the Pale Watch. Welcome to the last town before Hearthglen.

Before I send anybody up that road, I want them to have seen it with their own eyes. People hear 'the Crusade' and think of a few zealots with torches. Go and look at the walls, and the towers, and the people on them.

Out the gate and straight up the King's Road. You'll see the gate long before you reach it. Don't draw steel, and don't let them get a good look at your face. Then come back down and tell me what you saw.
quests.turn_in_text:
So now you've seen it. Walls, towers, and a lot of people who'd like to burn you.

I was a police officer in Hamburg, back home. I've raided worse places, but never with a sword.

quests.title: Sentries on the Road
quests.description: Kill Scarlet Sentries on the road and in the fields below Hearthglen.
quests.accept_text:
Every Scarlet Sentry on the road below Hearthglen turns back anyone who isn't wearing red. That was fine while they stayed up there. Lately they've been coming down at night, closer every time, and last night one of them was close enough to read our gate.

Push them back up the hill, north of here. They stand in pairs on the road and in the fields under the gate. They'll call for help if they can, so don't let one run. Keep it quick and keep it quiet.
quests.turn_in_text:
That'll keep them on their own side of the hill for a while.

Hale used to be a security contractor, back on Earth. He knows what an open flank looks like, and so do I.

quests.title: Crossbows on the Wall
quests.description: Kill the Scarlet Crossbowmen hiding in the hedges and ditches below Hearthglen.
quests.accept_text:
Hearthglen's answered us. With the sentries gone, they've put a Scarlet Crossbowman in every hedge along the road. One of Mateo's scouts took a bolt yesterday from a hedgerow he'd walked past a hundred times.

I want them out of the fields north of here. They hide in the hedges and the ditches below the walls. A crossbow takes a while to wind and they know you know it, so close the distance fast and don't stand still in the open.
quests.turn_in_text:
Mateo's scout is going to live, and the fields are ours to walk again.

I've got something for Rory, if you're heading south.

quests.title: Word from the Watch
quests.description: Carry Lena's report to Flamekeeper Rory Callahan in the Order's quarter of the Bulwark.

objectives.label: Bring Lena's report to Flamekeeper Rory Callahan at the Bulwark

quests.accept_text:
I've watched Hearthglen's gate for a month, and I've written down everything I've seen. Hale is pulling his people in behind the walls. Patrols, wagons, the lumber crews from Northridge. I don't think he's planning to sit behind those walls. I think he's getting ready to come out of them.

Rory needs this. He's at the Bulwark now, at the keep in the Order's quarter on the south side of the street. Fly if you can, the roostkeeper's by the south wall. Give it to Rory and wait while he reads it, because he'll have an answer.
quests.turn_in_text:
Lena's report, in her lovely tidy hand. She writes like she's filling out a form.

Hale's getting ready to march. I knew he would. Tell Lena to hold the Watch, and that I'm coming north.

on_accept.name: Lena's Report
on_accept.description: A thick report in a neat hand, with a sketch of Hearthglen's gate on the back of the last page.

quests.title: A Letter for Brill
quests.description: Carry Lena's letter to Flamewarden Teodor Novak in Brill.

objectives.label: Bring Lena's letter to Flamewarden Teodor Novak in Brill

quests.accept_text:
The Order keeps a man in Brill. Flamewarden Teodor Novak watches the Scarlet Monastery from a window over the inn, and he's very good at it.

If Hale marches out of Hearthglen, the Monastery marches with him. Teodor needs to know what I know, and he needs to know it from me.

Go south to the Bulwark and out its west gate into Tirisfal, then on to Brill. Teodor lodges over the inn. He'll offer you a drink, and you should take it. It's the only good beer in Tirisfal.
quests.turn_in_text:
Lena's writing to me? Then it's bad.

I was a firefighter in Brno, back home, and I know what it looks like when two fires are about to join up. Tell her I'll keep my eyes on the Monastery.

on_accept.name: Lena's Letter
on_accept.description: A short letter sealed with the Pale Flame, addressed to Brill in a tidy hand.

quests.title: Worgs on the Road
quests.description: Kill Rotting Worgs on the roads round the Pale Watch.
quests.accept_text:
I'm Mateo, and I keep the Watch's roads open, and the Rotting Worgs have worked out that the road is where the food walks.

They run in packs and they don't let go once they've got you. I've had two runners come in with half a leg each this week.

They work the roads south and west of the gate, mostly at dusk. Break the packs up. Don't fight more than two at once, and keep moving, because they go for your legs.
quests.turn_in_text:
That's a road I can walk at dusk again.

I taught kids to ride horses outside Rosario, back home. Out here the horses are dead and the dogs want to eat me.

quests.title: Skeletal Wanderers
quests.description: Kill Skeletal Wanderers on the roads of North WPL.
quests.accept_text:
The Skeletal Wanderers walk the roads with nowhere to go. I think they were travellers once, caught on the road when the plague came, and they've just kept walking ever since.

They're slow, but there are a lot of them, and they never stop. When they see you they turn round and follow, all of them, until you're backed against something.

They gather on the roads. Clear them off, and don't let them pin you against a wall.
quests.turn_in_text:
Thank you. I hated watching them walk.

They were going somewhere, once. I suppose we all were.

quests.title: Down to the River
quests.description: Find a safe way down to the Thondroril's bank, east of the Pale Watch.

objectives.label: Find a way down to the Thondroril's bank

quests.accept_text:
We haul every barrel of water up from the Thondroril, the river on the east side of the fields, and it's a long way round to the only path we trust.

I'd like a shorter one. Somewhere on the bank the dead don't use, where we can put a barrel at the bottom and a marker at the top.

Go east from the gate, through the fields and down to the river. Find somewhere quiet and stand on it. You'll know it when you see it, because nothing will be trying to eat you.
quests.turn_in_text:
That's a good path. We'll put a marker on it and a barrel at the bottom.

Oona's down there most days, fishing. Say hello if you see her.

quests.title: The Blighted Herd
quests.description: Kill Blighted Stags in the fields north and east of the Pale Watch.
quests.accept_text:
There's a herd of Blighted Stags in the fields north of the Watch. Most days they graze. When something spooks them they run, and they run straight at our walls, and twice now they've come through the gate before we could shut it.

I'd like the herd thinned before the third time. They graze in the fields north and east of the town. Don't stand in front of them when they bolt. Pick off the ones on the edge of the herd and let the rest run.
quests.turn_in_text:
Our gate's still on its hinges this morning, which is a first this week.

Take one of these. It's the least I can do.

quests.title: Travellers' Keepsakes
quests.description: Take Traveller's Keepsakes from the Skeletal Wanderers on the roads.
quests.accept_text:
I can't stop thinking about the Skeletal Wanderers. If they were travellers, they had pockets, and some of them still have whatever was in them. A ring, a letter, a toy for somebody waiting at home.

I'd like to write down what they were. Somebody might still be waiting for one of them, and the Order keeps a book of names at the Bulwark.

They walk the roads all round the Watch. Not every one of them has anything left. Bring me what you find and I'll write it all down.
quests.turn_in_text:
A pipe, a thimble, a child's wooden horse. Every one of these belonged to somebody.

Odile at the Bulwark will want these for her book. I'll send them south.

quests.title: Riverbank Ghouls
quests.description: Kill Riverbank Ghouls in the reeds along the Thondroril.
quests.accept_text:
I'm Noah, and I patch up whoever makes it back through the gate. Lately that's been people who went down to the river.

The Riverbank Ghouls hide in the reeds along the Thondroril and drag people into the water. The ones who come back have bites I can't keep clean.

They lie on the banks east of the town and come at you out of the water. Stay on the high ground and let them climb to you.
quests.turn_in_text:
Nobody came in from the river with bites today. That's a good day.

I was a nurse in Winnipeg, back home, and I've never been happier to have nothing to do.

quests.title: Sludge Samples
quests.description: Collect Cauldron Sludge Samples from the Cauldron Sludges at Gahrron's Withering.
quests.accept_text:
There's a cauldron at Gahrron's Withering, east of here. The Cauldron Sludge that crawls out of that cauldron is the plague at its purest, near enough, and that's exactly what I want.

I think I can make a serum. Not a cure, nothing that good, but something that slows the sickness long enough to get somebody to a priest. I need to start with the real thing.

The sludges crawl round the cauldron at the Withering. Kill one and scoop what's left into a jar. Keep the lid on tight and don't breathe it in.
quests.turn_in_text:
This is horrible. Thank you.

If I can make something from this that stops the sickness, every medic on both sides of the sea will want it.

quests.title: The Withering
quests.description: Kill Withering Ghouls and Withering Cultists at the cauldron in Gahrron's Withering.
quests.accept_text:
The cauldron at Gahrron's Withering is the Cult's. The Withering Cultists stir it, and the Withering Ghouls carry the plague out to the fields in buckets, like they're watering a crop.

I want that cauldron left with nobody to stir it.

It's east of the Watch, past the dead orchard. The cultists stand at the cauldron and the ghouls work round it. Kill the cultists first. They'll heal the rest, and I'd rather not be patching you up afterward.
quests.turn_in_text:
The cauldron's cold. That's one less in the Plaguelands.

There's someone in charge out there, though, and he isn't going to stay dead on his own.

quests.title: Gahrron the Withered
quests.description: Kill Gahrron the Withered at his farm.
quests.accept_text:
Gahrron owned the farm the Withering is named for. He died there, and the Cult raised him to guard their cauldron, and now Gahrron the Withered walks his own fields thinking they're still his.

I'd like him put to rest, so we can burn the place clean. It won't heal while he's walking it.

He's near the cauldron at Gahrron's Withering, north-east of here. He's slow, but he's strong, and the sickness comes off him in waves. Take friends, and take something for the nausea. I'll have more of it here when you get back.
quests.turn_in_text:
Then the Withering's done. We'll burn it in the morning.

He was a farmer. I keep thinking about that. He just wanted to keep his farm.

quests.title: A Serum for Felwood
quests.description: Carry Noah's Serum to Dr. Nkechi Adeyemi at the Emerald Sanctuary in Felwood.

objectives.label: Bring Noah's serum to Dr. Nkechi Adeyemi at the Emerald Sanctuary

quests.accept_text:
I made it. It doesn't cure anything, I want to be honest about that, but it slows the plague down long enough to matter.

There's a doctor at the Emerald Sanctuary in Felwood, Dr. Nkechi Adeyemi, who's treating a sickness that sounds a lot like this one. She sent me the kit I've been using all month. I'd like to send her something back.

Take the zeppelin from Tirisfal to Orgrimmar, then go north through Ashenvale to Felwood. The Sanctuary's the clean glade in the middle of it. Keep the vial out of the sun.
quests.turn_in_text:
A serum, from the Plaguelands? Let me see.

This is clever work. I was an emergency doctor in Lagos, back home, and I'd have been glad of this then. Tell him I'll try it on the felblight, and I'll write.

on_accept.name: Noah's Serum
on_accept.description: A small vial of pale green serum, wrapped in a bandage and labelled in careful capitals.

quests.title: The Inquisitors
quests.description: Kill Hearthglen Inquisitors in the fields below Hearthglen.
quests.accept_text:
I was a priestess in Hearthglen. When the Hearthglen Inquisitors started questioning the newcomers, I stood in the room while they did it. I held the candle. I didn't say a word.

Then one day I walked out, and I kept walking until I reached this town. I think I'm still walking.

The inquisitors go down into the fields north of here in pairs, looking for anyone to question. I want them stopped. They'll burn you if they can, so don't let them finish a prayer.
quests.turn_in_text:
I knew some of them. I prayed beside some of them.

I won't pretend I'm not glad they're gone. That's something I'll have to make peace with.

quests.title: The Confessions
quests.description: Take Signed Confessions from the Hearthglen Inquisitors.
quests.accept_text:
The inquisitors carry the confessions they've forced out of people, signed and sealed, so they can be read out before a burning. Every one of them has a name on it.

I'd like those names remembered by somebody who isn't going to burn them.

The Hearthglen Inquisitors walk the fields north of here, and they keep the confessions in their satchels. Not all of them will have one. Bring me whatever you find, and please don't read them. They aren't true, and the people who signed them knew it.
quests.turn_in_text:
Here's Agnieszka Nowak, and Tunde Bello, and Hyun-woo Park, and they didn't even spell them properly.

These people came here from nowhere and we burned them for it. I'll make sure they're remembered.

quests.title: The Book of Names
quests.description: Carry the Bundle of Confessions to Chaplain Odile Marchand at the Order's chapel in the Bulwark.

objectives.label: Bring the confessions to Chaplain Odile Marchand at the Bulwark

quests.accept_text:
Chaplain Odile Marchand keeps a book of names, everyone the Order knows of who died in the Plaguelands. She brought it down from Sorrow Hill when the Order moved into the Bulwark, and it's the only thing she carried herself.

I'd like the people in these confessions to go into her book. Their names should be somewhere other than Hearthglen's ledgers.

Go south to the Bulwark. The Order's chapel is on the south side of the street. Tell her they're from me, and that I'm sorry there are so many.
quests.turn_in_text:
These are from Amalie? She was in Hearthglen when these were taken.

I'll write every name in the book tonight. Some of them were from Lyon, you know. I knew one of these streets.

on_accept.name: Bundle of Confessions
on_accept.description: The inquisitors' confessions, tied with a ribbon Amalie took from her own habit.

quests.title: High Inquisitor Faulk
quests.description: Kill High Inquisitor Faulk and the Hearthglen Inquisitors who walk with him.
quests.accept_text:
High Inquisitor Faulk runs the inquisition at Hearthglen. I served under him. He's the one who decided the newcomers were the Scourge's agents, and he decided it on a Tuesday, between breakfast and prayers.

On feast days he walks the fields himself, with the Hearthglen Inquisitors at his back. Today's a feast day.

He'll be below the walls, close to the gate. He's got a temper and a lot of fire, and he heals himself when he's hurt. Bring friends, and bring someone who can stop his prayers.
quests.turn_in_text:
Then it's done, and the inquisition's got nobody to lead it.

I keep waiting to feel something. I think maybe I feel lighter.

quests.title: Northridge
quests.description: Kill Scarlet Lumberjacks and Scarlet Sawyers at Northridge Lumber Camp.
quests.accept_text:
I'm Jonah, and I built every wall in this town, and I built them out of green wood because it's all I could get.

The Crusade runs a lumber camp at Northridge, in the west, and the Scarlet Lumberjacks and Scarlet Sawyers up there cut the best oak in the north. All of it goes up the hill to Hearthglen.

I'd like the camp emptied. The lumberjacks are in the woods and the sawyers are at the mill. They're working men with axes, so don't underestimate them.
quests.turn_in_text:
That's the camp quiet, then. Now we can see about the wood.

I built houses in Duluth, back home. Long winters, good timber. This place reminds me of it, except for the dead.

quests.title: Woodsman Archers
quests.description: Kill Scarlet Woodsman Archers in the trees round Northridge.
quests.accept_text:
With the lumberjacks gone, the Crusade's sent Scarlet Woodsman Archers into Northridge's trees to guard the timber. They're good shots, and they know those woods better than I do.

I can't send wagons in while they're up there. They hide in the trees round the camp, north-west of here. Look up, because they like the high branches, and don't let them pin you down in the open.
quests.turn_in_text:
The woods are clear. My wagons go in tomorrow.

I'll need someone to pick out the good planks before the rest of them burn the lot.

quests.title: Seasoned Oak
quests.description: Take Seasoned Planks from the Scarlet Sawyers at the Northridge mill.
quests.accept_text:
The wall round the Watch is green wood, and it's started to warp. Another winter and I'll be able to post letters through the gaps.

The Scarlet Sawyers at Northridge, north-west of here, carry the camp's best seasoned planks to the carts. Seasoned oak won't warp. I want enough to rebuild the gate, at least.

Take the planks off the sawyers before they reach the carts. Look for Hearthglen's stamp, because that's the good stuff.
quests.turn_in_text:
Feel the weight of that. That's proper oak.

The gate will be up by the end of the week. I'd like to meet the man who's been running that camp, though.

quests.title: Foreman Harrow
quests.description: Kill Foreman Harrow at the mill in Northridge.
quests.accept_text:
Foreman Harrow runs Northridge for the Crusade. He's the one who sent the archers out, and he came back to the camp yesterday with a fresh crew.

As long as he's there, the camp fills up again every time we empty it.

He's at the mill in the middle of Northridge, north-west of here. He's a big man with a big axe, and he doesn't like visitors. Take friends with you.
quests.turn_in_text:
That's the end of Northridge for the Crusade.

The camp's ours now. I'll put a crew in there next month and we'll cut our own timber.

quests.title: Saw Blades
quests.description: Take Hearthglen Saw Blades from the Scarlet Lumberjacks at Northridge.
quests.accept_text:
I can't cut timber without saws, and the Crusade took every saw in the Plaguelands up to Northridge. I've been shaping planks with a hatchet, and it shows.

The Scarlet Lumberjacks carry good steel blades, forged in Hearthglen. They carry them on their backs in the woods.

Bring me the blades and leave the handles. I'll make my own handles. I'm a carpenter, not a smith.
quests.turn_in_text:
These are beautiful blades. Hearthglen's smiths know their business, I'll give them that.

We'll have a proper sawpit at the Watch by the end of the week.

quests.title: Snapjaws on the Thondroril
quests.description: Kill Thondroril Snapjaws on the banks of the Thondroril.
quests.accept_text:
I'm Oona, and I catch the Watch's supper. I fish the Thondroril, mostly, and the Thondroril Snapjaws keep taking my catch, and my lines, and once my boot.

They're big and they're mean, and nothing in that river has ever told them no.

They sun themselves on the banks east of the town. Watch out for the bite, because they don't let go. Stay out of the water.
quests.turn_in_text:
My lines will last the day now.

I fished out of Galway, back home. The fish here are different, but the patience is the same.

quests.title: Plague Bats
quests.description: Kill Plague Bats along the Thondroril.
quests.accept_text:
The Plague Bats come out over the Thondroril at dusk and dive at the water, and at me. I'm sure they carry the plague, and I'm tired of fighting them off with a fishing rod.

They roost in the trees along the river. They're fast, so don't chase them. Stand still on the bank and let them come to you, because they will.
quests.turn_in_text:
I can fish at dusk again. That's the best time for it.

Thank you. Take one of these, and I'll keep a fish back for you at supper.

quests.title: Antler Hooks
quests.description: Take Blighted Stag Antlers from the Blighted Stags in the fields.
quests.accept_text:
I've run out of hooks, and there's nowhere out here to buy them. I carve my own from antler, the way my grandfather taught me.

The Blighted Stags in the fields have antlers that are still sound under the grime, because I've checked.

They graze north and east of the town. Bring me the tines, not the whole rack. I don't need a rack, I need hooks.
quests.turn_in_text:
These will carve beautifully.

My grandfather taught me this on the beach at Salthill, back home. I never thought I'd need it.

quests.title: Old Thondroril
quests.description: Kill Old Thondroril and the Thondroril Snapjaws round his pool.
quests.accept_text:
There's one snapjaw in the Thondroril I've never been able to move. Old Thondroril is older than the plague and bigger than a cart, and the Thondroril Snapjaws follow him round like he's their king.

He sits on the deep pools, where the big fish are. I've been looking at those fish for months.

He keeps to the deepest pool and comes up when he's hungry. Kill the young ones while you wait. Stay on the bank, because he's stronger in the water.
quests.turn_in_text:
The deep pools are mine now. Look at the size of the fish down there.

You'll eat well at the Pale Watch tonight, and every night after.

quests.title: The Patrol Roster
quests.description: Take the Hearthglen Patrol Roster from a Scarlet Sentry below Hearthglen.
quests.accept_text:
I'm Wendel, and I kept Hearthglen's books until I read what I was writing down, and then I left. I still keep books. It's an old habit.

The Scarlet Sentries carry the week's roster, which tells everyone where to stand on the walls. If I had a copy, the Watch would know those walls as well as I used to.

The sentries on the road north of here, below the gate, carry it in a leather case at the belt. Bring it back dry, please. The ink runs.
quests.turn_in_text:
This is in Brother Jessup's hand. I'd know his capitals anywhere.

The newcomers here always ask how I can read the walls from a page. It's just bookkeeping, really.

quests.title: Hearthglen's Hounds
quests.description: Kill Scarlet War Hounds in the fields below Hearthglen.
quests.accept_text:
The roster says Hearthglen sends its Scarlet War Hounds out at night, to hunt anyone near the walls. I used to feed those dogs. They were good dogs, once. They'd sit for a crust.

They aren't good dogs any more. They're what Hearthglen made them.

They hunt the fields north of here, below the walls, at night and in packs. Don't let them circle you. Back up against something and let them come.
quests.turn_in_text:
They were good dogs once. I used to give them the scraps from the kitchen.

That's done, then. Thank you. I'll write it down, because somebody should.

quests.title: The Water Under the Hill
quests.description: Kill Cave Drowned and Seepwater Shades in the Weeping Cave, in the hill above the Thondroril.
quests.accept_text:
I've fished the Thondroril every day since the Watch went up, and the river's gone wrong. There's water running into it out of the hill, and it tastes of the grave. The fish won't go near it.

It's coming out of the Weeping Cave. Something in there keeps the water moving, the Cave Drowned and the Seepwater Shades, I'm told.

The cave's in the hill on the east side, up above the river. You'll hear it before you see it, because the water never stops running down the walls. Mind your feet in there. It's slick all the way down.
quests.turn_in_text:
The fish'll come back now, give it a week.

There's a cave like that on the coast near Galway, back home. The water ran out of it clean. I never thought I'd miss a cave.

quests.title: The Weeper
quests.description: Put the Weeper to rest at the pool at the end of the Weeping Cave.
quests.accept_text:
Oona told me about the water out of the Weeping Cave, and I know the story behind it. I wish I didn't.

When Hearthglen took a family for questioning, the mother went looking for them. She went into the cave because somebody told her they'd been taken out that way. She went into the pool at the end of it, and she never came out. The Weeper is her. I'm nearly sure of it.

The pool's at the far end of the cave, past both galleries. She'll know you're coming, because she's been waiting for somebody for years. Be gentle if you can, and be quick if you can't.
quests.turn_in_text:
Thank you. I'll write her name in the chapel book, under the ones Hearthglen never wrote down.

I kept quiet in that room for a long time. I'm trying to make up for it, one name at a time.

quests.title: The Hermit's Account
quests.description: Kill the Drowned Hermit in his cell in the roof of the Weeping Cave.
quests.accept_text:
I remember every name in Hearthglen's ledgers, and one of them belonged to a hermit who lived in the cave above the river. He paid his tithe in fish, every quarter, for eleven years.

When the plague came, the Crusade stopped taking his fish, and he stopped coming down. I'm told The Drowned Hermit still keeps his cell in the roof of the Weeping Cave, and that he won't let anyone past.

His cell's up through the roof of the upper gallery, about halfway along. He'll have his oar, I expect. He never went anywhere without it. Close his account for me, would you?
quests.turn_in_text:
Tobias Fenn, paid in perch every quarter for eleven years. I'll mark him settled.

It's a small thing, closing an account properly. Somebody ought to do it for everyone Hearthglen forgot.

quests.title: Supplies from Felwood
quests.description: Carry Dr. Adeyemi's Field Kit to Field Medic Noah Kowal at the Pale Watch in North WPL.

objectives.label: Bring Dr. Adeyemi's field kit to Field Medic Noah Kowal at the Pale Watch

quests.accept_text:
I've heard from the Order of the Pale Flame that their field medic at the Pale Watch is stitching people up with thread he boils in a pot. I was an emergency doctor in Lagos. I know exactly what that means.

So I've packed everything the Sanctuary can spare. Sutures, dressings, a bottle of something strong.

It's a long way, I know. Get yourself to the Eastern Kingdoms, through Tirisfal to the Bulwark, and keep going north up the King's Road. The Pale Watch's gate is off the road where it starts to climb toward Hearthglen. Don't let anyone ration the sutures.
quests.turn_in_text:
Real sutures, clean dressings, and a bottle of something I haven't seen since Winnipeg.

Tell Dr. Adeyemi she's saved more people today than I've managed all month. Then come back, because I've got work for you.

on_accept.name: Dr. Adeyemi's Field Kit
on_accept.description: A canvas roll of sutures, dressings and small brown bottles, packed tight and labelled in English.

quests.title: Closing Hearthglen's Books
quests.description: Kill Grand Crusader Victor Hale in Mardenholde Keep, above Hearthglen.
quests.accept_text:
I kept the ledgers in Hearthglen for eleven years. I know what the Crusade spends and what it burns, and I know who signs for both.

Grand Crusader Victor Hale signs for both. He commands Hearthglen from Mardenholde Keep, up the hill past the town, and every order that sends a patrol south to burn a farm comes from his desk.

I walked out with nothing but my pen. Go up to the keep and close his books for him. You'll have to go through the town first, and the town won't let you pass quietly.
quests.turn_in_text:
Then the account's closed. I'll write it in my own hand, with the date.

The Crusade will keep ledgers somewhere else. I'll learn where.

quests.title: The Infirmary
quests.description: Kill Chirurgeon Maeve Ostrowski and High Clerist Hendrick in Hearthglen.
quests.accept_text:
I'm Beatriz Couto. I ran a cafe in Porto before the Integration, and now I run the last bed before Hearthglen, so I hear what comes out of it.

What comes out of the infirmary is screaming. Chirurgeon Maeve Ostrowski cuts newcomers open to look for the plague, and she never finds it, and she keeps looking. High Clerist Hendrick stands at the door and blesses the work.

Two of my guests came out of that infirmary. One of them still can't hold a cup. Go into Hearthglen and stop them both, please.
quests.turn_in_text:
Thank you. I'll tell my guests in the morning, over coffee. Well, what passes for coffee.

Your bed's free here for as long as you want it.

quests.title: The Kennels
quests.description: Kill Huntsman Radley and Hearthglen Mastiffs in Hearthglen.
quests.accept_text:
My hawks won't fly over Hearthglen, and I know why. The Crusade keeps hounds there, and the hounds are trained to run down anyone who flees the town.

Huntsman Radley keeps the kennels. He breeds the Hearthglen Mastiffs himself and sends them after anyone who runs, and he's proud of how few get away. I trained sheepdogs in Donegal before the Integration. What he does to his dogs makes me sick.

Go into the town, kill him and his mastiffs, and give the next runner a chance.
quests.turn_in_text:
Then the next one who runs might reach us. That's all I wanted.

The hawks still won't fly over it. Give them time. Give me time too.
